messages:
maya: Quick retro/check-in after the recurring Friday-02:45 UTC p95 spikes. Root cause seems to be cross-zone cache stampede + a small routing bias. We need: SLO eval window updates, a dashboard that highlights fallback activations, and owners for remediation. Proposals: 1) change p95 eval window from 5m->1h for trend detection but keep short-window guardrails at 5m, 2) add fallback-activation timeseries + last-fallback-reason tag, 3) alert earlier on error-budget burn (10m window). Claim items: A) SLO policy + migration notes, B) dashboard + alerts, C) runbook playbook + quick checks, D) routing/auto-rebalancer fix. Please claim by EOD.

trent: I can take A. Will prepare a draft SLO PR that implements dual-eval windows: long-window for reporting (1h) and short-window for paging (5m). Will include migration notes for Dedicated customers. ETA PR: Tue EOD.

maya: Nice. Dual-window approach should help avoid noisy rollups while keeping fast detection.

gabe: I'll pick B. Plan: new dashboard row: fallback activations (counter) with `last_fallback_reason` label, p95 short-window sparkline (5m), and a 1h trend panel. Alert: `sum(increase(fallback_activations_total[10m])) by (region) > 3` -> page eng-sre. Will also add links from panels -> runbook anchors.

gabe: example promql for fallback panel: `sum(increase(fallback_activations_total[5m])) by (cluster,reason)`

gabe: ETA staging dash: Thu.

ivy: Ill take C. Runbook additions: quick cache eviction checks, command to force route to warm pool, and a small play called "02:45 spike": a checklist + decision tree. Will include exact commands and a rollback anchor.

ivy: runbook snippet:
```
# check evictions in last 10m
curl -s "https://metrics/api/v1/query?query=sum(increase(cache_evictions_total[10m]))"
# force warm pool routing
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://deploy.internal/api/v1/routes/override -d '{"policy":"warm-pool"}'
```

maya: Thanks. D is open.

trent: Small question: when we change reporting windows, do we need to update our SLA docs? Customers often look at p95 without knowing evaluation windows.

maya: Yes, include a customer-facing blurb in the migration note. Well stage the SLO change in canary for 72h and collect fallback trigger counts before wider rollout.

gabe: I'll add a small widget that shows canary vs global p95 to help decide rollout.

ivy: Runbook will include a section "Canary review checklist" with exact metrics to inspect: fallback rate, cache_miss_ratio, p95 delta.

slo-bot: IncidentBot: postmortem draft created -> https://infra/reports/2199000001 at 2199000100

maya: Assigning owners & due dates in action tracker:
- trent: SLO PR + migration docs  due 2026-04-07
- gabe: dashboards + alerts + canary comparison panel  due 2026-04-05
- ivy: runbook + 02:45 spike playbook  due 2026-04-03
- unassigned: routing/rebalancer fix  please volunteer by EOD

trent: I'll put the SLO PR as draft and include the canary rollout plan. Also add a short FAQ for CS about evaluation windows.

gabe: Staging dashboard pushed at 2199000200 (dash-staging-v3). Link: https://dash.staging/2199000001

ivy: Runbook PR opened -> https://git.internal/r/redwood/runbooks/pulls/321. Contains 02:45 playbook and curl commands.

maya: If no one picks D by EOD I'll take it, but prefer ops to own routing changes. Also let's add a metric `rebalancer_actions_total` so we can see corrective events over time.

trent: Note to self: include migration note that explains why p95 long-window helps with trend smoothing and examples on interpreting the two windows.

gabe: Will add panel links to the runbook anchors so oncall can jump from page to play.

slo-bot: DeployTracker: staging dashboards deployed at 2199000200 (dash-staging-v3)
